  • like court orders.
  • • The Council protects freedom of the press and encourages responsible journalism.
  • • It helps maintain public confidence in media and ensures accountability in reporting.
  • • The Press Council acts as a watchdog balancing press freedom with responsibility and
  • ethical standards

questions.question: Descibe the provisions of the Cable Television Networks Act, 1995 related to programme code, advertisement code and compulsory transmission of channels / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• No person shall transmit or re-transmit through a cable service any programme or advertisement
  • unless such programme or advertisement as the case may be is in conformity with the prescribed
  • programme or advertisement code. Programme code – (1) No programme should be carried in cable
  • service which: i) offends against good taste or decency ii) contains criticism of friendly countries iii)
  • contains anything obscene, defamatory, deliberate, false iv) contains anything amounting to contempt
  • of court v) denigrates children vi) is not suitable for public exhibition etc. (2) The cable operator should
  • strive to carry programmes in his cable service which project women in a positive, leadership role of
  • sobriety, moral and character building qualities. (3) No cable operator shall carry or include in his cable
  • service any programme in respect of which copyright subsists unless he has been granted a licence by
  • owners of copyright.(4) Care should be taken to ensure that programmes meant for children do not
  • contain any bad language or explicit scenes of violence. Programmes unsuitable for children must not
  • carried in the cable service at times when the largest numbers of children are viewing. (5) No cable
  • operator shall include in his cable service any channel, which has not been registered by the Central
  • Government for being viewed within the territory of India.
  • Advertisement code – (1) No advertisement shall be permitted which: i) derides any race, caste,
  • colour, creed and nationality ii) is against any provision of the Constitution of India iii) tends to incite
  • people to crime, violence etc. iv) exploits the national emblem or any part of the Constitution
  • v) projects a derogatory image of women vii) exploits social evils like dowry, child marriage
  • vi) promotes the production, sale or consumption of cigarettes, tobacco products, wine, alcohol, infant
  • milk substitutes, feeding bottle or infant foods. (2) Advertisements must not be directed towards any
  • religious or political end. (3) The picture and the audible matter of the advertisement shall not be
  • excessively ‘loud’. (4) Advertisement which endangers the safety of children or shows them in an
  • undignified or indecent manner shall not be carried in the cable service. (5) No programme shall carry
  • advertisements exceeding twelve minutes per hour. (6) Indecent, vulgar or offensive themes or
  • treatment shall be avoided in all advertisements.
  • Compulsory Transmission of Channels – Every cable operator shall re-transmit i) channels operated
  • by or on behalf of the Parliament of India ii) at least two Doordarshan terrestrial channels and iii) one
  • regional language channel of a State in the prime band. It is also the duty of the cable operator to ensure
  • that his cable television network does not interfere with the functioning of the authorised
  • telecommunication systems.

questions.question: Write notes on the following i) In camera proceedings ii) Fair and accurate report of judicial proceedings iii) Media trial / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• In-camera proceedings are court sessions held privately , without the presence of the public or
  • media. A person shall be guilty of contempt of court for publishing the text or a fair and accurate
  • summary of the whole or any part of an order made by a court sitting in chambers or in camera, if the
  • court has expressly prohibited the publication on grounds of public policy, public order or security of
  • state or on the ground that it contains information relating to a secret process, discovery, invention etc.
  • In camera proceedings are usually followed in sexual offences, family disputes, national security cases
  • etc.
  • A fair and accurate report of judicial proceedings refers to the responsible and unbiased coverage
  • of court cases by the media, ensuring that the information published is factually correct and balanced. A
  • fair and accurate report of judicial proceedings, a fair criticism of a judicial act in the interest of the
  • public good, and a bonafide complaint concerning the presiding officer of a subordinate court do not
  • constitute contempt of court. A judgement can be criticised as erroneous, but dishonesty on the part of
  • the judge in delivering the judgement cannot be alleged.
  • Trial by newspapers has been considered by courts as interference with the proper administration of
  • justice in pending cases. Media trial refers to the influence of media coverage on public opinion about a
  • person or case before a court verdict is delivered. It occurs when the press or television channel s
  • present their own version of events, often passing judgment before the legal process is complete. Judges
  • and witnesses may be indirectly influenced by public opinion shaped by the media.

questions.question: Illustrate your arguments regarding the abolition of Official Secrets Act / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Illustrate your arguments regarding the abolition of the Official Secrets Act
  • • The Official Secrets Act, 1923 was enacted during British rule to protect
  • confidential government information.
  • • The Act aims to prevent leakage of sensitive official information related to the
  • government
  • • Many argue that the Act is colonial in nature and outdated in modern
  • democratic society.
  • • It is criticised for restricting freedom of press and freedom of expression.
  • • The Act is considered inconsistent with the Right to Information Act, which
  • promotes transparency and public access to information..
  • • Critics argue that the Act has been misused to suppress investigative
  • journalism and whistle-blowers.
  • • Lack of clear definition of “secret information” creates ambiguity and misuse.
  • • Supporters argue that the Act is necessary for protecting national security.
  • • It helps prevent espionage, spying, and leakage of confidential information.
  • • The Act safeguards defence, intelligence, and strategic operations of the
  • country.
  • • Many experts suggest reform rather than complete abolition of the Act
  • • There is a need to replace it with a modern law ensuring both transparency
  • and security..
  • • Classified and confidential information should be clearly defined.
  • • A balance must be maintained between national security and democratic
  • accountability.
  • • Many suggest reforming the Act to protect both citizens’ right to information
  • and the security interests of the nation.

questions.question: Write notes on the following i) Central Board of Film Certification ii) Advisory Panels iii) Suspension and revocation of certificate / [CO5] [15x2 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• The Central Board of Film Certification commonly known as the Censor Board is a statutory
  • body under the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Government of India . It is responsible for
  • regulating the public exhibition of films in India. Functions of the Board: i) Preview and examine films
  • before release ii) Grants appropriate certificates or suggests modifications or cuts before certification.
  • iii) Enforce guidelines for the certification iv) Prevent obscene or harmful content.
  • Advisory Panels are supporting bodies formed under the Central Board of Film Certification to help in
  • the examination and certification of films. These panels play a key role in reviewing and
  • recommending the type of certificate a film should receive . The examining committee shall consist of
  • a member of the advisory panel and an examining officer either of whom shall be a woman in the case
  • of a short film and four members of the advisory panel and an examining officer of whom two persons
  • shall be women in the case of a long film.
  • Suspension and Revocation of Certificate - The Central Government may, by notification in the
  • Official Gazette, suspend a certificate granted under this Act or may revoke such certificate if it is
  • satisfied that: i) the film in respect of which the certificate was granted, was being exhibited in a form
  • other than the one in which it was certified; or ii) the film or any part thereof is being exhibited in
  • contravention of the provisions of this Act. Any person aggrieved by any order under this Section, he
  • may within sixty days from the date of its publication in the Official Gazette, make an application to the
  • Central Government for review of the order. On receipt of the application, the Government may, after
  • giving the aggrieved person a reasonable opportunity of being heard and after making such further
  • enquiry, pass such order confirming, modifying or reversing its decision and the Board shall dispose of
  • the matter in conformity with such order.
  • (2x15=30)

questions.question: Discuss the main provisions in the Cinematoraph Act, 1952 / [CO5] [15x2 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss the main provisions in the Cinematograph Act, 1952.
  • • The Cinematograph Act, 1952 regulates certification and exhibition of films in
  • India.
  • • The Act provides legal control over public exhibition of films.
  • • Films are certified by the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC).
  • • The CBFC examines films before public release.
  • • Categories of film certification include: U – Universal viewing, UA – Parental
  • guidance for children, A – Adults only, S – Restricted to a specific class of
  • persons
  • • Certification may be refused or cuts may be ordered if film:
  • Threaten national security
  • Affect public order
  • Harm morality or decency
  • Promote obscenity or excessive violence
  • • The government has power to revise, suspend, or review certification in
  • certain situations
  • • The Act also regulates cinema theatres through licensing procedures.
  • • Safety standards and conditions for exhibition of films are maintained under
  • the Act.
  • • The Act helps protect public morality, social values, and cultural interests.
  • • It attempts to balance creative freedom of filmmakers with public interest
  • and social responsibility.
  • • The Act remains an important legislation regulating film certification and
  • exhibition in India
